```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4)
set.seed(1)
```

regcompR fits distributional regression models: every parameter of a
response distribution can depend on covariates through its own formula. The
same model specification can be fitted by maximum likelihood (`engine =
"ml"`), through TMB (`"tmb"`), or by Bayesian inference in Stan, JAGS or
OpenBUGS (`"bayes"`).

```{r}
library(regcompR)
```

## Distributions

Every family lives in a registry that records its support, parameters,
links, moments and references.

```{r}
length(families())
head(families("count"), 10)
d <- distribution("gamma", mu = 2, sigma = 0.5)
prob(d, c(1, 2, 3))
quantile(d, c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9))
plot(d)
```

## A first regression

The first formula is the main formula (it models the mean parameter, or
the location or scale parameter where there is no mean). Further formulas
name the parameter on their left side.

```{r}
n <- 400
dat <- data.frame(x = runif(n), z = rnorm(n))
dat$y <- rgamma(n, shape = 1 / (0.3 + 0.4 * dat$x)^2,
                scale = exp(1 + dat$x) * (0.3 + 0.4 * dat$x)^2)
fit <- regcomp(y ~ x, sigma ~ x, family = "gamma", data = dat)
summary(fit)
```

## Specifying the model

* `links =` changes the link of a parameter (`links()` lists them);
* `fixed =` holds a parameter at a known value;
* `weights =` multiplies each log likelihood contribution;
* `subset =` selects rows (a logical or index vector);
* data parameters (trial counts, known minima) are given by name, as
  `size = n` for the binomial;
* `offset()` enters a term with coefficient one;
* `parameterization =` chooses among parameterizations of a law
  (`get_family("gamma", "rate")`);
* `y ~ .` uses every other column.

```{r}
f_link <- regcomp(y ~ x, sigma ~ 1, family = "gamma", data = dat, links = list(mu = "identity"))
f_fix <- regcomp(y ~ x, family = "gamma", data = dat, fixed = list(sigma = 0.5))
f_sub <- regcomp(y ~ x, family = "gamma", data = dat, subset = dat$x > 0.2, weights = rep(2, n))
f_rate <- regcomp(y ~ x, family = "gamma", parameterization = "rate", data = dat)
names(coef(f_rate))
bd <- data.frame(n = rpois(50, 10) + 1, x = rnorm(50))
bd$k <- rbinom(50, bd$n, plogis(0.3 * bd$x))
coef(regcomp(k ~ x, family = "binomial", size = n, data = bd))
```

Rows with a missing or non finite value in anything the model evaluates
(the response, a transformed covariate such as `log(x)`, a weight or a data
parameter) are left out, as with `glm()`. The fit stores its analysis rows,
and cross validation and clustered covariances use exactly those rows.

```{r}
dm <- dat; dm$x[3] <- NA; dm$z[5] <- -1
fm <- regcomp(y ~ x + log(z + 1), family = "gamma", data = dm)
nobs(fm)
head(fm$rows)
```

`regcomp_control()` sets the optimizer (`maxit`, `rel_tol`, `restarts`,
`start` values), the Laplace inner problem, the proximal solver of lasso
type penalties and the MCMC settings.

```{r}
f_ctl <- regcomp(y ~ x, family = "gamma", data = dat,
                 control = regcomp_control(restarts = 2, start = list(mu = c(1, 1))))
f_ctl$diagnostics[c("converged", "max_abs_gradient")]
```

## Methods for fitted models

```{r}
coef(fit)
sqrt(diag(vcov(fit)))
confint(fit)
logLik(fit); AIC(fit); BIC(fit); nobs(fit)
formula(fit)
head(fitted(fit))
```

`residuals()` gives randomized quantile (`"quantile"`, the default),
`"pit"`, `"response"` and `"pearson"` residuals.

```{r}
sapply(c("quantile", "pit", "response", "pearson"), function(t) round(head(residuals(fit, type = t), 3), 3))
```

## Predictions

`predict()` returns the distribution parameters (`"parameter"`), the linear
predictors (`"link"`), `"mean"`, `"variance"`, `"sd"`, `"median"`,
`"quantile"`, `"probability"` (mass or density at `at`), `"density"`,
`"cdf"` and `"survival"`, with optional confidence intervals.

```{r}
nd <- data.frame(x = c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9))
predict(fit, nd, type = "parameter")
predict(fit, nd, type = "link")
predict(fit, nd, type = "mean", interval = "confidence")
predict(fit, nd, type = "variance")
predict(fit, nd, type = "sd")
predict(fit, nd, type = "median")
predict(fit, nd, type = "quantile", probs = c(0.05, 0.95))
predict(fit, nd, type = "density", at = 5)
predict(fit, nd, type = "cdf", at = 5)
predict(fit, nd, type = "survival", at = 5)
```

`fitted_distribution()` returns the fitted law of each row as a
distribution object; `simulate()` draws new responses; `log_lik()` gives
pointwise log likelihoods.

```{r}
fd <- fitted_distribution(fit, nd)
quantile(fd, 0.9)
dim(simulate(fit, nsim = 3))
head(log_lik(fit))
```

## Checking the fit

```{r}
plot(fit, which = "qq")
plot(fit, which = "effects", variable = "x", par = "sigma")
```

## Where to go next

* `vignette("distributions")`: the registry and distribution objects.
* `vignette("operators")`: inflation, hurdles, mixtures, truncation, generated families and custom families.
* `vignette("count-models")`: overdispersion, zeros and the count families.
* `vignette("hierarchical-longitudinal")`: random effects, covariance structures, smooth terms, GEE and nonlinear (mixed) models.
* `vignette("ordinal-categorical")`: ordinal, nominal, bivariate binary and selection models.
* `vignette("survival")`: censoring, truncation, cure models, Cox and frailty models and discrete time hazards.
* `vignette("regularization")`: penalized and bias reduced estimation.
* `vignette("model-checking")`: residuals, scoring rules, cross validation and comparison.
* `vignette("reporting")`: regression tables, tidy output and export of tables and plots.
* `vignette("bayesian")`: priors, generated Stan and BUGS programs and Bayesian fitting.
